emma: Heads up — I got an email from the plan vendor that they're migrating platforms next week. If there9s a cutover week where contributions land late, will employees lose the employer match for that pay period? Worried about timing because some folks have pay increases/deferral changes this month.

liz-peopleops: Good question. During vendor cutovers we treat payroll deposits as the source of truth. If the vendor receives the deposit late but it was withheld by payroll in the correct pay period, we work with them to ensure the match calculation uses the payroll date. That said, there are edge cases where the vendor's processing window can affect reporting.

jake-eng: Can we get a formal escalation path? If someone9s match is missed, what9s the fix cadence?

dana-hr: Process we follow: (1) employee files ticket to benefits@redwood, (2) we open a vendor case and provide payroll trace file, (3) vendor requests an adjustment; most corrections post within 1-2 payroll cycles. If the vendor says no, we can do a manual company-side corrective contribution but that requires exec approval for material amounts.

vendor-ops: From vendor side 30 heads up: During the migration batch windows shrink to 24-48h. Any files received after the window may be applied to the next processing cycle which can show as a late deposit. Submit sample payroll trace with payroll run id and withhold amounts so we can map deposits.

emma: Thanks. Also second part: a teammate asked if changing HSA pre-tax payroll elections during open enrollment affects 401(k) match or contribution limits in any way? They're considering moving more pre-tax into HSA.

liz-peopleops: HSA contributions are separate from 401(k) deferrals and do not reduce the 401(k) match calculation directly. Match is typically a percentage of eligible payroll deferrals (pre-tax + Roth 401k combined in our plan). But check plan language: some plans tie match to deferral types; ours counts both pre-tax and Roth basics. HSA is a cafeteria pre-tax benefit but does not count toward 401(k) deferral base.

payroll-bot: Reminder: Open enrollment for benefits closes 2026-05-12 11:59PM PT. Final payroll cutoff for changes affecting 2026-05-29 pay is 2026-05-20 12:00PM PT.

jake-eng: One more: our colleague still has an outstanding 401(k) loan and the vendor migration notice said loans may not be transferable. If vendor A -> vendor B, do outstanding loans carry over or turn into a distribution?

dana-hr: We requested written confirmation from the vendor. Typical outcomes: vendor B accepts loan records and continues amortization, or vendor B treats outstanding loans as terminated and presents options (repay in full, offset as taxable distribution, or set up repayment plan). We will publish guidance after migration cutover and will proactively contact employees with loans.

emma: Appreciate the clarity. Can benefits/people-ops post a short FAQ and a template ticket for payroll traces so managers know what to attach? :pray:

liz-peopleops: Yep — we'll publish a 1-pager and a premade email containing the payroll run id, pay date, employee SSN last 4, gross/net/deferrals. I'll drop the doc in #people-ops and link in the vendor migration announcement.

vendor-ops: If anyone wants to test a sample trace before migration, DM and we9ll replay it against our staging pipeline. :gear:
